description:
## Destination

A written verdict on defk (`docs/verdict.md`). It covers a set of target workloads taken from the jobs people really write NIFs for, each in the catalog with an honest verdict against an optimised Elixir baseline. It also defines a kernel subset (language and runtime contract) good enough to express those workloads, with a developer experience where a kernel author can predict what is allowed and gets actionable errors when it isn't. The subset reference lives in `docs/language.md`. It is written so it could grow into a Hex library later; no packaging work happens now.

## Notes

- Domain: research into native kernels for Elixir. Glossary in `CONTEXT.md`; purpose and measurement rules in `AGENTS.md` and `examples/README.md`.
- Every session consults the skills "grilling" and "domain-modeling" (and "research" / "prototype" for those ticket types).
- Elixir first: defk only where it helps. Optimise and measure the Elixir side before claiming a defk win. Elixir wins are valid verdicts.
- Scope is demand-driven: a language feature, type or convenience construct is in only when a target workload needs it. Convenience constructs must be what an Elixir developer writes first, cost nothing over the hand loop, and keep Elixir's meaning.
- Devex bar for done: actionable compile errors (line, why, alternative); a subset reference with every divergence; one rule a developer can keep in their head ("Elixir over these types, with Elixir's results, or a compile error").
- Pinned: no arbitrary-precision integers (i64 overflow stays `ArithmeticError`). Runtime contract is done apart from hardening and the question of state kept between calls.
- This map holds decisions. Build work stays in the existing beadwork roadmap (README "Roadmap"); the map points at it, it doesn't own it.

## Decisions so far

- [Where does Nx already cover native-speed numerics for Elixir?](defk-dtw.2): Nx owns whole-tensor numerics on large fixed-shape arrays; defk's niche is sequential/early-exit loops, variable-length byte work, and many concurrent mid-sized calls that must stay preemptible (no Nx backend yields).

## Not yet specified

- **Language additions per workload.** Once the target workload set is chosen: which types (`f32`, `[f32]`, `[i32]`/`[u16]`, 2-D arrays, fixed-shape records), which byte-level binary constructs (`<<>>` matching on fixed fields, building output binaries), and which convenience constructs (`|>`, `Enum.sum/max/min` over arrays, indexed generators, module attributes as constants, `for ... into:` an allocated array, multi-clause kernels) each workload needs.
- **Equivalence checking.** How "Elixir's results" is verified across the subset (property tests against Elixir?) depends on whether kernels can run as Elixir.
- **Which runtime hardening is required for done** versus nice to have (stats across reloads, frame layout tags, hang-proof resume tests).
- **The stance on needing a C compiler at compile time**, as it bears on the verdict and on any future library.
- **Catalog coverage plan.** Which new catalog entries and baseline optimisations the verdict needs, handed off as build tickets. Includes at least one kernel written in Elixir, defk and `defn`+EXLA, to measure EXLA-CPU per-call latency and `while` cost (open from the Nx boundary research).

## Out of scope

- Hex packaging, precompiled NIFs, and a semver promise (destination is a verdict that could grow into a library).
- Editor support: LSP diagnostics, formatter.
- UTF-8 strings as text, and maps (provisional: reopen only if the workload survey demands it, which redraws the destination).
- Calling back into Elixir from a kernel; concurrency inside a kernel.
- An upstream proposal to Elixir core or ERTS.
title: Wayfinder: roadmap to a defk verdict (kernel subset, runtime contract, devex)
